messages:
maria_support: Hey team — customer reports rerank endpoint returning very strange scores after they mixed embeddings from two different embedding models. They claim top result scores are >1.0 and order is nonsensical. Attaching their repro payload and the error/response they got.

maria_support: customer excerpt — 
```
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "query_embedding": [0.12, 0.03, ...],          # 768-d vector from model 'embed-lite-768'
  "candidate_embeddings": [
    {"id":"a","embedding":[0.01,0.02,...]},  # 1536-d from 'embed-large-1536'
    {"id":"b","embedding":[...]}              # 1536-d
  ]
}
```
They didn't get an explicit 400; the endpoint returned scores but they were all tiny negative and some >1. Response snippet: 
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{
  "results": [
    {"id":"a","score":1.23},
    {"id":"b","score":-0.12}
  ]
}
```
They also saw no error in logs. Customer says they always paired embeddings from different models because they thought rerank internally normalizes.

sam_sre: @maria_support thanks — this screams dimension/model mismatch. rerank expects same-dim vectors produced by a single embedding model (or at least same vector size and normalization). If you feed mixed dims the internal dot/metric math will produce garbage or trigger implicit padding/truncation depending on runtime path. Do we have their exact embedding lengths?

maria_support: They pasted counts: query len = 768, candidate lens = 1536. Customer used 'embed-lite-768' for queries and precomputed candidate vectors with 'embed-large-1536'.

pj_engineer: Repro plan: I can run a quick local call to the rerank model with mismatched dims to see deterministic behavior. But first, tell them to run a sanity check: compute dims and a small dot product locally. Example check we ask customers to run: 
```
# python quick check
import numpy as np
q = np.random.rand(768)
c = np.random.rand(1536)
# try naive dot -> will raise or silently do wrong depending on code
try:
  print(np.dot(q, c))
except Exception as e:
  print('dot failed', e)
```
If their client libraries silently cast/pad, that could explain non-error 200 with nonsensical scores.

maria_support: They ran local dot and got a ValueError (shapes not aligned). But the POST to rerank returned results instead of an error.

sam_sre: That suggests our API layer is accepting mixed shapes and then invoking a fallback path that projects vectors (badly). We should consider returning 4xx on size mismatch. For now, mitigation for customer: recompute candidate embeddings with the same model as query or vice versa. Provide them a safe helper: 
```
# quick curl to verify dims via embeddings endpoint
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings/check \  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \  -d '{"model":"embed-large-1536","input":"test"}' | jq '.embedding | length'
```
That returns expected vector length. Ask them to run for both models and confirm.

maria_support: Customer ran the above: embed-lite-768 -> 768, embed-large-1536 -> 1536. They want a workaround because recomputing 500k candidates is expensive.

pj_engineer: Workarounds we can suggest (ranked by reliability):
1) Recompute query embeddings with the same model used by candidates (cheap).
2) Recompute a small subset of candidates and test quality.
3) If recomputing all candidates is impossible, provide a compatibility conversion script: not ideal, but you can upsample/concat zeros or downsample by averaging blocks — BUT warn: this changes semantics and will degrade ranking. Example naive pad to 1536: 
```
# pad query 768 -> 1536
q1536 = np.concatenate([q768, np.zeros(768)])
```
We must explicitly tell customers this is lossy and unsupported.

ops-bot: deployment-notice: We have a known internal path where mixed-dim vectors hit the vector-store adapter which will attempt implicit conversion for legacy projects. Filed issue INF-4523.

sam_sre: INF-4523 — temporary fix: enforce strict validation at API surface. I'll open a small patch to return 400 with a helpful message when dims mismatch. For customer-facing messaging include: 
- error code: 400_BAD_REQUEST
- message: "embedding dimension mismatch: query length 768 vs candidate length 1536. Ensure embeddings come from same model or same dimensionality."

jamie_product: +1 for clear error. Also: can we add a console warning in the Dashboard when uploading candidate embeddings with model metadata mismatch vs project default? Reduce this support load.

maria_support: Customer also flagged billing/time concerns — they were charged for many trial rerank calls while trying to debug. They asked for a credit. Should we escalate to billing?

eng-oncall: If we can reproduce a server-side bug that accepted invalid payloads, billing should consider a credit. Please capture request_id and request timestamps. Ask the customer for the rerank call IDs and I will correlate.

pj_engineer: I ran a local repro against staging with mixed dims. Staging behavior: we returned 200 and scores; logs show warning in worker: "vector_len_mismatch -> implicit_projection used" and a stack trace showing adapter path. I attached the staging log lines to the ticket.

maria_support: Shared logs and staging request IDs with customer; asked them to run one test that we can pick up: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d '{
  "query_embedding": [<768 numbers>],
  "candidate_embeddings": [{"id":"a","embedding": [<1536 numbers>]}]
}'
```
and reply with request-id header from response.

sam_sre: Action items: 
- pj: patch API validation to 400 on mismatch, add clear error message (INF-4523). Priority P0.
- eng-oncall: check billing policy for accidental runs due to server-side acceptance and propose one-time credit if customer provides request ids.
- jamie: product explore dashboard warning when uploaded embedding artifacts model metadata != project default.
- maria: share recommended workaround (recompute query or pad with zeros as last resort) and ask for request ids.

pj_engineer: Quick repro note for internal: when candidate dim > query dim we hit vector-store adapter that zero-pads query; when candidate dim < query dim we truncate. Both produce nondeterministic ranking and inflated scores. We'll remove implicit pad/truncate and replace with explicit validation and guidance.

maria_support: Customer accepted workaround to recompute query embeddings to 1536 for a small test bucket and will send request ids for billing. They appreciate the patch plan. 

sam_sre: Thanks team. I'll own the patch and roll a hotfix to staging + prod once reviewed. Please add cross-link to INF-4523 in the ticket. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: INF-4523 created by sam_sre at 2026-03-15T14:22:10Z.

maria_support: Closing loop with customer now. If billing OKs credit we'll update thread.

pj_engineer: Note for release: document in "Rerank best practices" that embeddings must be same-model/same-dimension; include a migration guide for large candidate sets (batch recompute + checkpointing).

maria_support: End.
